subject: Proof of Readiness checklist, acceptance tests, and close plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Peter Lang <peter@oaklinehealth.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@oaklinehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@oaklinehealth.com
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proof of Readiness checklist, acceptance tests, and close plan

Hi Peter & Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a concise "proof-of-readiness" checklist that maps the evaluation tasks to explicit acceptance tests, exit gates, and the suggested close timeline so your procurement and engineering teams can validate readiness without ambiguity. Attached: POF_Readiness_CHECKLIST_v1.xlsx and a short test-case appendix (Oakline-Eval-Test-Cases.pdf).

High-level proposal:
- 4-week evaluation window starting next Monday (Mar 8)
- Acceptance criteria: functional (>=95% intent match on sample set), latency (95th percentile <= 650ms for 512 token prompt), and reliability (error rate <0.5% during test load)
- Exit gates: tech signoff (Engineering), compliance signoff (Procurement/security), and business signoff (Product owner)

Would you confirm: 1) the evaluation window dates work, and 2) whether the latency target needs to be tighter for any specific flows? If you want, I can slot a short call with procurement to review the compliance checklist.

If this looks ok I can post a MAP in HubSpot and add owners for each acceptance test so we can close by Apr 5 assuming green signals.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Sales — Redwood Inference
(attachment: POF_Readiness_CHECKLIST_v1.xlsx)
(attachment: Oakline-Eval-Test-Cases.pdf)

From: Peter Lang <peter@oaklinehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@oaklinehealth.com>, procurement@oaklinehealth.com
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proof of Readiness checklist, acceptance tests, and close plan

On Thu, Mar 4, 2027 at 9:12 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Peter & Sofia —
> 
> Thanks again for the demo yesterday...

Thanks Vivek — this is a very helpful starting point. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we circulate to our engineering and procurement teams: 

1) The functional acceptance metric — when you say "">=95% intent match on sample set" can you confirm the sample size and whether that counts paraphrase tolerance? We need to know the evaluation harness details so our QA can reproduce results.
2) Latency target: for clinician-facing flows we prefer 400ms p95 when the prompt length is under 256 tokens; for batch background jobs the 650ms p95 is fine. Can we split the SLA per flow?
3) Procurement: can you attach the data retention and logging spec that maps to your compliance page? procurement@oaklinehealth.com is on cc.

If you can respond by EOW we’ll aim to start the window next Monday as suggested.

Best,
Peter Lang
Director of Product — Oakline Health
(attachment: none)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Peter Lang <peter@oaklinehealth.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@oaklinehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@oaklinehealth.com
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proof of Readiness checklist, acceptance tests, and close plan

Peter —

Thanks, great questions. Quick answers inline and I’ve attached an updated MAP and a short evaluation harness note (MAP-Oakline-v2.xlsx).

1) Sample size and tolerance: our proposed test set is 1,200 prompts (300 per major use-case). The 95% intent-match uses a fuzzy-match tolerance that we’ll share as part of the harness (thresholds and scorer included in MAP-Oakline-v2). We'll hand over the harness so your QA can run locally and reproduce scoring.
2) SLA by flow: absolutely. I split the acceptance tests into two buckets: clinician-interactive (p95 <= 400ms @ <256 tokens) and background/batch (p95 <= 650ms). Both have separate test vectors in the PDF appendix.
3) Data retention/logging: attached a short compliance extract in the updated MAP and linked our compliance page for details. Key items: 30-day ephemeral KV cache, option for customer-managed keys (KMS), and audit logs exported daily.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm owners for each gate (engineering lead, procurement owner, product owner) — I can add them to the MAP and assign tasks.
- We run a smoke-run day (Mar 10) to validate integration and baseline metrics, then start the full evaluation on Mar 11.

If that timeline works I’ll push the MAP into HS-28921 and share an action tracker.

Thanks — attaching MAP-Oakline-v2.xlsx and reiterating the eval-test appendix.

Vivek
(attachment: MAP-Oakline-v2.xlsx)
(attachment: Oakline-Eval-Test-Cases.pdf)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Oakline MAP — pricing checklist & acceptance test owners (please review)

Marissa / Ben —

Looping you in here to align on the commercial and acceptance ownership before I finalize the MAP with Oakline. Key asks:
- Confirm whether we should propose a 3-month committed discount if Oakline signs by Apr 5 (suggested concession: 15% off list for first quarter).
- Review the acceptance tests in MAP-Oakline-v2 (I attached to the external thread) and flag any tests that should be added/removed — particularly around concurrency (50 concurrent clinician sessions) and token-level cost thresholds.
- Recommend owners: Engineering owner = Marissa (technical signoff), Procurement lead = Ben (commercial/compliance), Customer PO = Peter (external).

Please reply with one-line approvals or edits so I can fold into the final document.

Thanks,
Vivek

[internal note: Marissa — if we push a smoke-run Mar 10 we need Eng SRE on standby (Tues-Wed) and a small test harness from Carlos; can you confirm availability?)

From: Peter Lang <peter@oaklinehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@oaklinehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@oaklinehealth.com
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 11:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proof of Readiness checklist, acceptance tests, and close plan

Vivek —

All good progress here. Procurement reviewed the compliance extract and needs one tweak: since clinician data is PHI, Oakline legal requires a maximum of 14-day ephemeral cache (not 30). Can Redwood confirm support for 14-day retention or provide a compensating control (e.g., stricter redaction and SOC2 evidence)?

On performance: we agree to the two-bucket SLA (400ms/650ms). For concurrency, we want a slightly higher concurrency target during peak validation: 75 concurrent clinician sessions for the smoke day and 50 for normal acceptance runs. Please confirm whether that changes pricing materially (Ben/Marissa are cc'd).

If Redwood can confirm the cache retention adjustment and concurrency, we’ll sign the MAP and route to procurement for a formal PO.

Thanks,
Peter

(quoted)
> On Fri, Mar 5, 2027 at 8:30 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Peter —
> > 
> > Thanks, great questions...

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Peter Lang <peter@oaklinehealth.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@oaklinehealth.com>, procurement@oaklinehealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proof of Readiness checklist, acceptance tests, and close plan

Peter —

Thanks for the quick review and the procurement note. Confirmations and final items below: 

1) Cache retention: we can support a 14-day ephemeral KV cache for PHI-tagged flows. We'll enable stricter redaction and provide a SOC2 sub-set export during the evaluation window. I’ve added the required text to the final MAP (attached).
2) Concurrency target: we can support the smoke-day peak of 75 concurrent clinician sessions. Pricing impact: Ben recommends a one-time smoke-day capacity surcharge of $X (we'll include as cost line item in the MAP) — Ben, please confirm exact line, but this will not change the base unit pricing in the evaluation.
3) Timeline & signoff: smoke-run on Mar 10 (75 concurrency), full evaluation March 11–Apr 1, target sign by Apr 5 pending green signals on acceptance tests.

Attached: MAP-Oakline-Final.xlsx (includes the 14-day retention clause, acceptance test owners, and the HS-28921 link). Requesting procurement to review and confirm PO process. Once procurement confirms, we'll schedule a 30-minute close call on Mar 12 to sign the MAP and review the PO template.

Next steps (action items):
- Peter: confirm PO path & legal contacts (procurement).
- Marissa: confirm SRE standby and test harness ownership for Mar 10 smoke run.
- Ben: confirm the smoke-day capacity surcharge line item and provide a short invoice template.
- Neha: publish the MAP into HubSpot (HS-28921) and add acceptance-test owners as tasks.

Appreciate everyone's quick turnaround — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Sales — Redwood Inference
(attachment: MAP-Oakline-Final.xlsx)
